senses.gloss:
cikitsā
(‘desire to get rid of disease’)
------------------------------------------
Āyurveda, the science of health and longevity, is an ancient discipline. It purports to treat, not the disease as such, but the patient himself. In the process of making the patient recover his health and enabling him to live long, curative treatment is only one of the steps.
Out of the ‘aṣṭāṅgas’ or eight limbs of this science, ‘cikitsā’ or treatment of the disease, forms the sixth. It has four pādas or quarters: vaidya (the physician), औषध (the medicine), paricāraka (the nurse) and rogi (the patient).
The vaidya should be an adept in this science, not only in theory but also in practice. He should be devoted to his profession and of righteous conduct.
The औषध must be prepared by the vaidya himself after proper examination of the patient and diagnosis, with the right kind of materials.
The paricāraka must be meticulous, hardworking and sympathetic towards the patient.
The rogi should obey the commands of the physician and cooperate strictly with the paricāraka.
If these conditions are fulfilled, treatment will be effective.
See also ĀYURVEDA.
